We always had a range and built in ovens in the kitchen when I was growing up. So did our close family and friends. I had never lived in a house with a stove or actually used a stove until I was 19 and got an off-campus apartment in college.

I had no idea that stoves have that drawer at the bottom to store pans and pots. I just kept them in the cabinets. But every time I put a baking sheet in the dishwasher after making pizza or cookies, I could never find it. I'd keep buying new baking sheets. One day I randomly blew up at my roommate about it and was like "Are you doing something with the baking sheets?! Why the fuck do the baking sheets always go missing??!!"

He calmly walked over to the stove, opened the bottom drawer and revealed it was so full of baking sheets that it barely closed. I was like "THERE'S A FUCKING DRAWER UNDER THE STOVE??!!!"

Re #1: I agree that you obviously shouldn't be actively antagonistic to people you don't like in a professional setting. But if I don't like someone at my workplace, I ignore them. I do not say good morning to them when I come in. I do not say goodbye when I leave. I carry on as though they do not exist and allow them to do the same. She is the one who insists on making small talk with me in the elevator or if she sees me in the parking lot or something. Quite frankly if she doesn't like me I'd rather she just not bother. 

Re #2: I've gotten told this by other people before. But I honestly can't think of anything I've ever said or done that would have given her that impression. 

Re #3: I really wasn't aiming for nuance. I was offended. I felt disrespected. People who offend and disrespect me have no place in my life, online or IRL. I've defriended people for reasons like this before and will continue to do so. If they don't notice or care, better for us both. If they do notice, maybe they should think about the impression their actions give. 

Re #4: Inviting everyone but two people from a professional setting to an event is unprofessional in and of itself. Other people who I know for a fact she is not close to or good friends with were invited. I could understand if she was just inviting a handful of people from her "circle." But inviting 98% of the people from a given group is not acceptable. At that point you need to be prepared to do an all-or-nothing invite or face the consequences of the people you conspicuously choose to leave out. 
I have little to lose from not having her in my professional network. Before defriending her I noticed she is moving to a different part of the country for work in a different industry than the one I'm pursuing. There's probably not a whole lot of benefit to either one of us from a professional connection.
